terms.gloss: fine linen, a linen garment; here, a sarong
evidence: Curt. 8.9: corpora ūsque pedēs carbasō vēlant
terms.comment: Fine linen, and a garment made of it; Curtius uses it of the Indians, who wrap their bodies in linen down to the feet and bind their heads with linen cloths. The word for a sarong is the classical one used of a modern thing, and ours. How it is worn can be said plainly: carbasum circum lumbōs convolvere, a description of ours (see the examples).

phrases.latin: Corpora ūsque pedēs carbasō vēlant; soleīs pedēs, capita linteīs vinciunt
phrases.english: They cover their bodies down to the feet with linen and their feet with sandals, and bind their heads with linen cloths
Put on your sarong; we’re going into the temple.

phrases.latin: Carbasum circum lumbōs convolve et cingulō astringe.
phrases.english: Wrap the sarong round your waist and tie it with the sash.
